cards.explanation: The answer is the house of the LORD. Hananiah, a prophet from Gibeon, speaks up there, with the priests and all the people right in the room. He says it to Jeremiah, the prophet, with everybody listening. That's like announcing your big news in the group chat instead of sending one text.

The missing word is "broken." Hananiah says, "I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon." Jeremiah has been wearing a yoke as a sign (Jeremiah 27:2), so a message about a broken yoke lands right in front of him. Hananiah brings it as good news, friends.

The answer is within two years. Hananiah says, "Within two years I will restore to this place all the articles of the house of the LORD…" Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had carried them off to Babylon. Notice Hananiah puts a time limit on it, not a vague "someday."

The answer is True. Hananiah says the LORD will restore Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, along with all the exiles from Judah who went to Babylon. Jeconiah was one of the people carried off (Jeremiah 27:20). Hananiah's promise list keeps growing, friends: articles, a king, all the exiles.

The answer is True. The first thing out of Jeremiah's mouth is "Amen!" He goes on, "May the LORD do so!" I bet that surprised some folks in the crowd, since the two prophets sound like they're on opposite teams.

The missing word is "true." Jeremiah says the prophet who prophesies peace will be recognized "…only if the word of the prophet comes true…" as the one the LORD has truly sent. That's the test, friends. It isn't how loud the prophet is or how good the news sounds.

The answer is that he breaks it. Hananiah "…took the yoke off the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke it." Snap, in front of everybody. His message was already about a broken yoke, since he had said, "I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon." Now he acts it out.

The missing word is "nations." Hananiah says the LORD will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, "…off the neck of all the nations." This isn't only about Judah anymore, friends. He's talking big.

The answer is False. After Hananiah breaks the yoke, Jeremiah goes on his way. Only shortly after does the word of the LORD come to him. I'd have had a whole speech ready, which is why I'm glad I'm not Jeremiah.

The answer is a yoke of iron. The LORD says, "You have broken a yoke of wood, but in its place you have fashioned a yoke of iron." Wood to iron is an upgrade nobody asked for. Hananiah's yoke is gone, and what replaces it is harder.

The missing word is "lie." Jeremiah says, "Listen, Hananiah! The LORD did not send you, but you have persuaded this people to trust in a lie." That's a serious charge, friends. The people were trusting something, and Jeremiah says it was a lie.

The answer is this year. The LORD says, "You will die this year because you have preached rebellion against the LORD." And the text tells us that in the seventh month of that very year, Hananiah died. I think this is a heavy part, friends, and it's okay to feel that.
